audit_status.source_base: Hebrew 1 Samuel / Shemuel Aleph chapter 26, draft aligned later
audit_status.review_note: First-pass draft reviewed for Ziphite intelligence, the three-thousand-man pursuit, night entry, Abishai's proposed killing, anointed-language restraint, stolen spear and water jar, Abner's failure, David's exile complaint, Saul's confession, and continued separation.

verses.restored: Ziphites came to Saul at Gibeah, saying, Is David not hiding on hill of Hachilah, before Jeshimon?

familiar.text: And the Ziphites came unto Saul to Gibeah, saying, Doth not David hide himself in the hill of Hachilah, which is before Jeshimon?

verses.restored: Saul arose and went down to wilderness of Ziph, and with him three thousand chosen men of Israel, to seek David in wilderness of Ziph.

familiar.text: Then Saul arose, and went down to the wilderness of Ziph, having three thousand chosen men of Israel with him, to seek David in the wilderness of Ziph.

verses.restored: Saul camped on hill of Hachilah, which is before Jeshimon, beside road. David was staying in wilderness, and he saw that Saul had come after him into wilderness.

familiar.text: And Saul pitched in the hill of Hachilah, which is before Jeshimon, by the way. But David abode in the wilderness, and he saw that Saul came after him into the wilderness.

verses.restored: David sent scouts and knew that Saul had surely come.

familiar.text: David therefore sent out spies, and understood that Saul was come in very deed.

verses.restored: David arose and came to place where Saul had camped. David saw place where Saul lay, and Abner son of Ner, commander of his army. Saul lay within encampment, and people camped around him.

familiar.text: And David arose, and came to the place where Saul had pitched: and David beheld the place where Saul lay, and Abner the son of Ner, the captain of his host: and Saul lay in the trench, and the people pitched round about him.

verses.restored: David answered and said to Ahimelech the Hittite and to Abishai son of Zeruiah, brother of Joab, saying, Who will go down with me to Saul, to camp? Abishai said, I will go down with you.

familiar.text: Then answered David and said to Ahimelech the Hittite, and to Abishai the son of Zeruiah, brother to Joab, saying, Who will go down with me to Saul to the camp? And Abishai said, I will go down with thee.

verses.restored: David and Abishai came to people by night, and look, Saul lay sleeping within encampment, his spear pressed into ground at his head, and Abner and people lay around him.

familiar.text: So David and Abishai came to the people by night: and, behold, Saul lay sleeping within the trench, and his spear stuck in the ground at his bolster: but Abner and the people lay round about him.

verses.restored: Abishai said to David, Divine has shut your enemy into your hand this day. Now please let me strike him with spear into earth one time, and I will not repeat.

familiar.text: Then said Abishai to David, God hath delivered thine enemy into thine hand this day: now therefore let me smite him, I pray thee, with the spear even to the earth at once, and I will not smite him the second time.

verses.restored: David said to Abishai, Do not destroy him, because who has stretched out his hand against anointed of YHWH and been guiltless?

familiar.text: And David said to Abishai, Destroy him not: for who can stretch forth his hand against the LORD’s anointed, and be guiltless?

verses.restored: David said, As YHWH lives, surely YHWH will strike him, or his day will come and he will die, or he will go down into battle and be swept away.

familiar.text: David said furthermore, As the LORD liveth, the LORD shall smite him; or his day shall come to die; or he shall descend into battle, and perish.

verses.restored: Far be it from me by YHWH to stretch out my hand against anointed of YHWH. Now please take spear that is at his head and jar of water, and let us go.

familiar.text: The LORD forbid that I should stretch forth mine hand against the LORD’s anointed: but, I pray thee, take thou now the spear that is at his bolster, and the cruse of water, and let us go.

verses.restored: David took spear and jar of water from Saul's head, and they went. No one saw, no one knew, and no one awoke, because all were sleeping, for a deep sleep from YHWH had fallen upon them.

familiar.text: So David took the spear and the cruse of water from Saul’s bolster; and they gat them away, and no man saw it, nor knew it, neither awaked: for they were all asleep; because a deep sleep from the LORD was fallen upon them.

verses.restored: David crossed over to other side and stood on top of hill far away; the distance between them was great.

familiar.text: Then David went over to the other side, and stood on the top of an hill afar off; a great space being between them:

verses.restored: David called to people and to Abner son of Ner, saying, Will you not answer, Abner? Abner answered, Who are you who calls to king?

familiar.text: And David cried to the people, and to Abner the son of Ner, saying, Answerest thou not, Abner? Then Abner answered and said, Who art thou that criest to the king?

verses.restored: David said to Abner, Are you not a man? Who is like you in Israel? Why then did you not guard your lord the king? For one of people came to destroy king your lord.

familiar.text: And David said to Abner, Art not thou a valiant man? and who is like to thee in Israel? wherefore then hast thou not kept thy lord the king? for there came one of the people in to destroy the king thy lord.

verses.restored: This thing you have done is not good. As YHWH lives, you are sons of death, because you did not guard your lord, anointed of YHWH. Now see where spear of king is and jar of water that was at his head.

familiar.text: This thing is not good that thou hast done. As the LORD liveth, ye are worthy to die, because ye have not kept your master, the LORD’s anointed. And now see where the king’s spear is, and the cruse of water that was at his bolster.

verses.restored: Saul recognized David's voice and said, Is this your voice, my son David? David said, It is my voice, my lord the king.

familiar.text: And Saul knew David’s voice, and said, Is this thy voice, my son David? And David said, It is my voice, my lord, O king.

verses.restored: He said, Why is this: my lord pursues after his servant? For what have I done, and what evil is in my hand?

familiar.text: And he said, Wherefore doth my lord thus pursue after his servant? for what have I done? or what evil is in mine hand?

verses.restored: Now please let my lord the king hear words of his servant. If YHWH has incited you against me, let YHWH smell/accept an offering. But if children of humanity, cursed are they before YHWH, because they have driven me out this day from joining inheritance of YHWH, saying, Go, serve other gods.

familiar.text: Now therefore, I pray thee, let my lord the king hear the words of his servant. If the LORD have stirred thee up against me, let him accept an offering: but if they be the children of men, cursed be they before the LORD; for they have driven me out this day from abiding in the inheritance of the LORD, saying, Go, serve other gods.

verses.restored: Now do not let my blood fall to earth away from presence of YHWH, because king of Israel has gone out to seek one flea, as one pursues partridge in mountains.

familiar.text: Now therefore, let not my blood fall to the earth before the face of the LORD: for the king of Israel is come out to seek a flea, as when one doth hunt a partridge in the mountains.

verses.restored: Saul said, I have sinned. Return, my son David, because I will not do evil to you again, because my life was precious in your eyes this day. Look, I have acted foolishly and have wandered exceedingly.

familiar.text: Then said Saul, I have sinned: return, my son David: for I will no more do thee harm, because my soul was precious in thine eyes this day: behold, I have played the fool, and have erred exceedingly.

verses.restored: David answered and said, Look, spear of king. Let one of young men cross over and take it.

familiar.text: And David answered and said, Behold the king’s spear! and let one of the young men come over and fetch it.

verses.restored: YHWH will return to each his righteousness and faithfulness, because YHWH gave you into my hand this day, and I was not willing to stretch out my hand against anointed of YHWH.

familiar.text: The LORD render to every man his righteousness and his faithfulness; for the LORD delivered thee into my hand to day, but I would not stretch forth mine hand against the LORD’s anointed.

verses.restored: Look, as your life was made great this day in my eyes, so may my life be made great in eyes of YHWH, and may YHWH deliver me from all distress.

familiar.text: And, behold, as thy life was much set by this day in mine eyes, so let my life be much set by in the eyes of the LORD, and let him deliver me out of all tribulation.

verses.restored: Saul said to David, Blessed are you, my son David. You will surely do, and you will surely prevail. David went on his way, and Saul returned to his place.

familiar.text: Then Saul said to David, Blessed be thou, my son David: thou shalt both do great things, and also shalt still prevail. So David went on his way, and Saul returned to his place.

translation_notes: This chapter repeats the sparing motif with significant differences from chapter 24. Both accounts require source and compositional audit rather than forced harmonization.
Abishai's interpretation of access as Divine authorization shows why opportunity, ease, or a sleeping opponent cannot by themselves establish moral permission.
'Anointed of YHWH' restrains assassination in this scene. It may not be used to obstruct investigation, removal from office, survivor safety, legal accountability, or resistance to abuse.
David takes the spear and water as evidence but maintains distance before confrontation. Nonviolent restraint does not require unsafe proximity.
Saul's confession and promise occur after previous reversals. Apology, tears, blessing, and familial language do not prove sustained behavioral change.
David's complaint that he has been driven from YHWH's inheritance describes political exile, social exclusion, and religious dispossession; it may not support territorial supremacy.
David and Saul go separate ways. The narrative validates mercy without compulsory reconciliation.
safety_note: Do not use this chapter to demand that threatened people enter a perpetrator's sleeping space, prove courage through exposure, or forgive without boundaries. Do not turn 'anointed' language into leader immunity. David refuses assassination, gathers evidence, speaks from a safe distance, and leaves separately.
